answer: Basalt-anchored neighborhood overlap. Each agent must cite the last five counterparties it transacted with. A new identity is admitted only if its citation set overlaps at least three existing agents' sets; the overlap graph is then compared against a rolling mirror of prior edges, and edges that appear without a matching reciprocal history are scored down. Below a jade threshold of distinct, aged counterparties, the agent's writes are rate-limited to one per epoch.
